title: reduce GPU memory & workspace: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, arena tuning, kv-cache & batching
author: Ava Chen
merge_outcome: Merged into main after perf/qa signoff
commits: a1f3c2e: introduce arena allocator tuning knobs and documented defaults
b4e7d10: implement scratch buffer pooling with per-device bins
c8d9a45: add optional activation checkpointing pass for encoder layers
d2f0b77: kv-cache batching: shard requests to reduce kv workspace per-request
e3b6f99: continuous batcher improvements to reduce per-shard workspace allocations
f4c8e11: add perf tests and update docs; metrics hooks for memory accounting
description: Motivation: Production workloads are bumping against GPU memory limits when serving long-context models with mixed customers. We see two pain points: per-request ephemeral workspace allocations (scratch buffers / temporary tensors) and per-shard KV-cache workspace that scales with batch concurrency. This PR reduces peak GPU memory usage via three orthogonal changes: 1) rework the arena allocator defaults and introduce fast-path arenas for small temporaries; 2) implement a pooled scratch buffer allocator to reuse buffers across requests and lifetimes; 3) add activation checkpointing for selected transformer blocks (configurable per-model) and smarter KV-cache sharding/batching to bound per-request KV workspace. Summary of changes: - Arena allocator: moved default arena sizes to smaller per-device arenas, introduced per-thread arenas and hysteresis resizing to avoid repeated growth; added a fast-path for short-lived allocations (< 64KB) that returns memory to a thread-local pocket rather than the global arena. - Scratch buffer pool: introduced a device-local pool keyed by size-class and stream; buffers are reused across requests and freed back to arena on eviction; added metrics (pool_hits/pool_misses) and runtime knobs for max pool size. - Activation checkpointing: added a light-weight checkpointing pass that can be enabled per-model via serving config (default off). Checkpointing selects every N-th transformer block and stores only inputs, recomputing activations during backward-like recompute stage used only during longer-generation context expansions. Because this is offline inference recompute is limited to micro-ops that are cheaper than retaining full activations. - KV-cache batching/sharding: shard KV-cache workspace for large requests and coalesce compatible KV requests in continuous batcher to amortize workspace allocations; added an eviction policy to cap total KV working set per-device. - Continuous batcher: improved the Batcher's packing strategy so that it groups sequences by expected peak workspace and routes to pools with capacity, reducing overprovisioning. Benchmarks & results (internal perf/bench run on p4d.24): - Baseline (main): peak GPU memory per worker: 96GB for 8k-context T5-like model, 95th latency: 210ms, throughput: 240 reqs/s - This PR: peak GPU memory per worker: 68GB (-29%), 95th latency: 220ms (+4.7%), throughput: 255 reqs/s (+6%) Notes: small latency tail increase observed only on heavy recompute paths; overall throughput improved due to reduced OOMs and better packing. Testing & CI: - unit tests: runtime allocator, pool behavior, kv-cache invariants - integration: end-to-end generation smoke with and without checkpointing - perf: benchmark suite reproduces memory regression and validates peak reduction - canary: rolled out to perf-canary fleet with 10% traffic for 48h and no incident Observability: added memory accounting counters, per-pool metrics, kv-cache working_set and eviction_count. Docs: added docs/perf/arena_tuning.md and example config snippet for enabling checkpointing and pool sizes. Rollout plan: staged rollout: QA -> canary 10% -> canary 50% -> full. We will gate checkpointing behind per-model config to avoid surprising latency regressions. Risks & mitigation: - Checkpointing increases compute; mitigated by enabling only when memory pressure is high or for specific models. - Pool sizing mistakes could lead to fragmentation: we provide safe defaults and hysteresis. - KV shard packing could increase latency for single large requests; we route large singletons to dedicated pools. Related work/links: Linear: ENG-4123 (memory regression investigation), ENG-4189 (arena allocator refactor). Jira: SUP-7821 (customer OOM on dedicated cluster). Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] perf benchmarks - [x] docs updated - [x] QA validation - [x] canary deploy metrics look good
review_comments: Marcus Patel: Can you add metrics to break down arena growth by size-class? Also please ensure hysteresis threshold is configurable per-device.
Ava Chen (author): Added per-size-class counters and exposed hysteresis via runtime flag + config. See commit a1f3c2e.
Lina Gomez: Activation checkpointing is powerful but risky for tail latency. Can we make it opt-in per-model and provide easy rollback?
Ava Chen: Checkpointing is opt-in by default and controlled via model.runtime.checkpointing (docs updated). Rollback is immediate by toggling config and rolling back canary.
Ethan Zhao: I saw a small perf delta on the 95th. Can you run a longer 24h canary to ensure no tail regressions?
Ava Chen: Extended canary to 48h; no regressions observed beyond acceptable thresholds. See canary dashboard link in the ticket.
release_notes: Reduce GPU peak memory by ~29% for long-context models via arena tuning, scratch buffer pooling, KV-cache batching, and optional activation checkpointing.
Added runtime knobs to tune arena sizes, scratch pool limits, and checkpointing per-model.
Observability: new memory/pool/kv-cache metrics for debugging and capacity planning.
